To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The proportion of college graduates entering professional occupations has fallen since 1970.
The proportion of college graduates working as professionals has been declining since the late 1970s, while the proportion of college educated Americans has been increasing.

1) the proportion of college educated workers in professional and managerial occupations has declined since the 1970s; 2) this decline is driven by a shift of college graduates into managerial occupations, not into other nonprofessional occupations; 3) the proportion of all workers who are college graduates has increased, but the proportion of college-educated workers in professional occupations has not; 4) this decline in college graduates in professional occupations is not due to a decline in the number of professional jobs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the changing position of professions in the U.S. economy, as reflected in the changing occupational distribution of college graduates.
the changing position of professional occupations in society, as reflected in the occupations of college-educated workers.
the changing occupational distribution of college graduates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proportion of college-educated workers entering professional occupations declined from 1950 to 2000.
the proportion of college educated workers entering the professions has declined.
the proportion of college-educated workers in professional occupations has fallen since 1950, but that this decline was more than offset by the rapid rise of the college-educated population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are in the midst of a major transformation of work in the US, but that this transformation has been much less dramatic than many have suggested.
while the economic returns for college graduates have increased, the number of college students aspiring to enter professional occupations has not kept pace.
we have a growing proportion of college graduates, who are increasingly working in managerial positions, but also increasingly working outside of professional and management work.

while the economic returns to college education have risen, the proportion of college educated Americans entering professional occupations has fallen.

the proportion of college students who aspire to enter professional occupations has declined over the last 30 years and this has not been replaced by increased aspirations towards managerial occupations.
